q.t: Two regular polygons have numbers of sides in the ratio 1 : 2 and interior angles in the ratio 3 : 4. How many sides does the smaller one have?
q.e: Angles (n − 2)/n and (2n − 2)/(2n) have ratio (n − 2)/(n − 1) = 3/4, so n = 5. Check: pentagon 108°, decagon 144°, and 108 : 144 = 3 : 4.

q.t: The exterior angles of a pentagon are x°, 2x°, 3x°, 4x° and 5x°. Find its smallest INTERIOR angle (in degrees).
q.e: 15x = 360, so x = 24. The largest exterior angle (120°) goes with the smallest interior angle: 180 − 120 = 60.
